postureOnlyComparisonToMain.mainSourceComparison: git diff56b700bc2..d6e9e57d6 for src/reach,src/watchglass and src/app/devices/reach was empty; original posture comparison remains source-valid.

preservedLimitations: Saved video includes old colored hand overlay; matching may benefit or suffer from that overlay.
Video frame and nearest raw result are not the same sensor exposure.
Bilinear resize via Sharp approximates browser Canvas; no new model inference or physical qualification.
Manual mode uses one explicitly human-selected finger tip at one selected frame with the same runtime whole-hand authority; it does not claim automatic finger recognition.

Automatic replay has 158 gesture-qualified tracking, 14 uncertain, 113 lost and 8 unseeded image observations across 293 saved frames; 5 source-ID change events remain. These precede Readiness, calibration and held-out validation and do not measure action reliability or universal automatic bridging.

The separate explicit hint diagnostic has 19 gesture-qualified tracking observations out of 24, 5 uncertain and 0 lost, with 0 source-ID changes. Pixels match on 23 frames, but 4 of those are withheld by whole-hand authority. This does not establish arbitrary-image finger recognition.

Earlier optical fallback, immediate-authority and pre-correction temporal diagnostics remain historical evidence of their own source identities. Earlier browser success never upgrades a later algorithm candidate.

Observed in-bounds model joints can still be misassigned. Current spatial compatibility and source-scoped three-frame/120ms confirmation prevent a single bad full-hand return from establishing persistent authority, without certifying physical gesture truth.
Raw posture qualification is separate from freshness, source association, sample stability and independent held-out accuracy.
Prompt labels indicate requested intent, not frame accuracy ground truth; no calibration was fitted from them.
The owner reported the sweep was not performed as intended; it is excluded from physical motion evidence.
Core CPU replay timings were measured under concurrent development load and are not hard timing bounds or physical capture-to-display latency.
No new physical webcam acceptance or held-out validation is claimed by these replay aggregates.
